kaps_punt: Leesvaardighede: lees met begrip en vlotheid: Lees oor die versorging van persone met VIGS: interpreteer/verduidelik en vertel wat aangeleer is

items.bewering: Sy leef met MIV. Die virus het haar liggaam se afweer baie swak gemaak. Die verpleegster by die kliniek het verduidelik dat sy daarom VIGS het.
items.bron: NC Department of Health and Human Services, HIV infection (testyourwell.nc.gov/cd/diseases/hiv.html): stage 3 (AIDS) is the most serious stage, when the immune system is so damaged it can no longer fend off infections; diagnosed by opportunistic infection or CD4 below 200. Healthline, HIV vs AIDS.

items.bewering: Die verpleegster by die kliniek het verduidelik dat sy daarom VIGS het (a clinic nurse diagnosing and starting her on treatment)
items.bron: Ten years of nurse-initiated antiretroviral treatment in South Africa, narrative review (PMC8007995): since 2010 professional nurses in South African primary care clinics diagnose, start and manage HIV patients on ART (NIMART).

items.bewering: Van daardie dag af het Tannie haar medisyne elke dag om dieselfde tyd gebruik.
items.bron: aidsmap, Adherence to HIV treatment (aidsmap.com/about-hiv/adherence-hiv-treatment): try to take pills at around the same time each day; NIH HIVinfo, Following an HIV treatment regimen: take HIV medicines every day, as scheduled.

items.bewering: Toe kon sy skaars van haar bed tot by die stoep loop ... Tannie het die hele pad self geloop en was skaars uitasem. "Die verpleegster sê ek is baie sterker as in die winter" (recovery over months on treatment)
items.bron: Medical News Today / Healthline HIV-AIDS summaries: antiretroviral therapy can raise the CD4 count until the person is no longer considered to have stage 3 HIV; NC DHHS HIV page. A recovery from very ill in winter to walking to the clinic some months later is consistent with this.

items.bewering: "Die MIV gaan nie weg nie. Maar die medisyne help my liggaam om sterk te bly"
items.bron: Healthline, HIV/AIDS (healthline.com/health/hiv-aids): there is no cure, no drug currently eliminates HIV from the body; antiretroviral therapy keeps HIV controlled and can restore the immune system.

items.bewering: Ma het gesê dat handskoene net nodig is as 'n mens aan bloed of ander vloeistowwe uit die liggaam raak. Dit geld byvoorbeeld by 'n wond en by beddegoed of klere wat daarmee vuil is.
items.bron: Napa County, HIV Transmission in Households (napacounty.gov/703): gloves during contact with blood or other body fluids; HealthLinkBC, HIV: tips for caregivers to avoid infection: gloves for blood and for cleaning items soiled with body fluids. Gloves are not needed for ordinary contact.

items.bewering: Ma het die handskoene aangetrek en die wond skoongemaak en toegedraai. Daarna het sy die vuil laken afgetrek en in 'n sak gesit. Sy het die handskoene uitgetrek en haar hande goed gewas.
items.bron: HealthLinkBC, HIV: tips for caregivers (healthlinkbc.ca/healthwise/hiv-tips-caregivers-avoid-infection): wash hands with soap and water after contact with blood even when gloves were worn; Alabama Department of Public Health home-care material: use disposable gloves for sheets soiled with blood and handle them as little as possible. Sources differ on how strictly soiled laundry must be separated, but the story claims no rule about it, only what Ma did, which matches every source.

items.bewering: "Vir 'n drukkie, 'n bord kos of 'n beker het ons dit nie nodig nie" / Sy het verduidelik dat MIV nie deur 'n drukkie, 'n beker of 'n bord kos oorgaan nie.
items.bron: CDC HIV FAQ, archived (webharvest.gov copy of cdc.gov/hiv/pubs/faq/faq31.htm): HIV is not transmitted by hugging, shaking hands or a casual kiss, nor by dishes, drinking glasses or food; HealthLinkBC, Ways HIV cannot be spread.

items.bewering: "My broer sê jy kry VIGS as jy uit jou tannie se beker drink" ... "Dit is nie waar nie"
items.bron: CDC HIV FAQ, archived (webharvest.gov): you cannot become infected from drinking glasses or dishes; saliva does not transmit HIV. The lesson presents the brother's claim as a myth and corrects it, which is correct.

items.bewering: Sy het ook gesê dat die virus deur bloed kan oorgaan en dat Ma daarom handskoene dra as daar bloed is.
items.bron: CDC HIV FAQ (archived) and HealthLinkBC: HIV is spread only through certain body fluids, blood among them; Napa County household guidance: gloves for contact with blood.

items.bewering: MIV: 'n Virus in die bloed wat die liggaam se afweer swakker maak.
items.bron: NC DHHS HIV page and Healthline HIV/AIDS: HIV is a virus that damages the immune system; it is carried in blood (and in certain other body fluids). The entry says 'in die bloed', not 'net in die bloed', so it does not exclude the other fluids.

items.bewering: VIGS: Wanneer MIV die liggaam se afweer teen siekte baie swak gemaak het.
items.bron: NC DHHS HIV page (testyourwell.nc.gov/cd/diseases/hiv.html): AIDS is the most serious stage of HIV infection, when the immune system is so damaged it can no longer fend off infections.

items.bewering: virus: 'n Baie klein ding wat net binne-in 'n liggaam skade kan doen.
items.bron: Dictionary.com, virus: an ultramicroscopic, metabolically inert infectious agent that replicates only within the cells of living hosts, mainly bacteria, plants and animals; Merriam-Webster learner entry: viruses grow and reproduce only inside living cells. Accurate at this level. 'Liggaam' leaves out plants and bacteria as hosts, which is a narrowing rather than a falsehood. Read alone the entry does not suggest a virus outside the body is harmless to touch, since it only does harm once it gets inside, which is consistent with the story's gloves.

items.bewering: kliniek: 'n Plek in die gemeenskap waar mense gesondheidsorg kry, of hulle siek is of gesond.
items.bron: GCIS South Africa Yearbook / Pocket Guide, Health (gcis.gov.za, 2003 and 2004): primary health care services at clinics include immunisation, maternity care, child screening and family planning, alongside treatment of illness; Western Cape Government health page lists family planning, baby immunisation and HIV testing. So healthy people also go to clinics.

items.bewering: medisyne: 'n Middel wat help om siekte of pyn te behandel, of om te keer dat 'n mens siek word.
items.bron: GEMET thesaurus (European Environment Agency), 'drug (medicine)': a substance used to prevent or treat disease or relieve pain; JSTOR knowledge graph, 'medication' (Q8403): a substance used to diagnose, cure, treat or prevent disease.

opsomming: Al 15 nagaanbare bewerings in die leesstuk en die vyf begrip-inskrywings klop met bronne. MIV gaan nie oor deur 'n drukkie, 'n beker of 'n bord kos nie, maar wel deur bloed. Handskoene is net nodig by bloed en liggaamsvloeistowwe, en daarna was 'n mens hande. MIV kan nie genees word nie, maar die medisyne help die liggaam om sterk te bly. Die les bevat geen oortreffende trappe en geen vergelykings nie.
